samples.summary: `--fresh` silently bypasses the newly-enforced 3-round bound and discards the carry-forward, so a 4th round can report as a clean round 1
samples.evidence: spec-to-pr.mjs:867 deletes every `round-N` directory and :878 then sets `const onDisk = args.fresh ? [] : roundsOnDisk(base)`, so `nextRound` returns 1 and `roundBoundNotice(1)` is "" — the refusal at :886–887 (`if (notice && !args.force) return fail(notice)`) never fires. `--force` is the advertised, noticed override (self-review.md: "The command **refuses** a fourth round; `--force` exists for the one case that earns it"), but `--fresh` reaches the same place with no warning at all AND additionally throws away every unfixed blocking finding (`priorFindingsFor(base, 1)` is never even called for round 1, spec-to-pr.mjs:900/930). The result a developer sees is `Local review panel: no blocking findings (round 1). The loop can stop here.` on a branch whose round-3 blockers were simply deleted — exactly the false negative the per-lens carry-forward exists to prevent. Either refuse `--fresh` past the bound the way `--force` is required, or at minimum print the bound notice when `--fresh` resets a base that already held `MAX_SELF_REVIEW_ROUNDS` rounds.

samples.summary: The design doc still states the removed warn-and-skip token contract for `spec-to-pr.mjs review`
samples.evidence: docs/design/harness-engineering.md:2403-2406 — "**Local review is a convenience, not authority:** `spec-to-pr.mjs review` runs the same lenses over the working diff, but needs `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` and degrades to a warn-and-skip when it is absent. The authoritative panel is still the cloud one". This diff deletes exactly that behaviour (`ambientAuthNotice` + the removed early return in `cmdReview`) and CLAUDE.md / CONTRIBUTING.md / agentic-dev-loop.md now say the opposite (local is the ONLY review an ordinary branch gets, and it runs on the ambient session and bills it). Nothing enforces prose accuracy in top-level design docs — the docs-refs lane only checks that backticked paths resolve — so this stale statement will persist and is the one a reader consults for the credential contract.

samples.summary: A sibling local SDK entry point still treats a missing `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` as a preflight problem, contradicting the ambient-session contract this change establishes
samples.evidence: scripts/agent/hunt.mjs:593-595 pushes `"CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN unset — run `claude setup-token` and export it"` into `problems`. `ambientAuthNotice`'s docblock (spec-to-pr.mjs:230-260) asserts the shared rule for the whole `ask.mjs` path: `createTokenPool` returns null for an empty pool, `buildSessionOptions` omits the `env` override, and the SDK resolves the logged-in session's own credentials. If that is true for the panel it is true for hunt.mjs, which goes through the same `ask.mjs`; the preflight now blocks (or at least loudly mis-reports) a local run that would work. Not broken by this diff, but it is the sibling site left out of step by it — fixing it here keeps one credential story rather than two.

samples.summary: The local carry-forward spreads raw `mergedFrom` members where the cloud projects and caps them, and the drift guard pins only the two selection filters
samples.evidence: `carryForwardFindings` projects the top-level finding but passes `mergedFrom: Array.isArray(f.mergedFrom) ? f.mergedFrom : undefined` through unchanged (prior-findings.mjs, the `.map(dropUndefined(...))` block). The cloud's inline copy at .github/workflows/agent-review-panel.yml:1028 projects each member to `{severity: norm(...), summary: trim(...,500), adjudication: {upheld}}` and slices to 5. So a locally-carried finding can hand the next round's verifier prompt arbitrary model-written keys and an unbounded list — the exact 'PROJECT, never spread' rule the function's own docblock states for the parent object. The new drift-guard test (prior-findings.test.mjs, "the panel workflow's inline copy applies both selection filters") only asserts the severity and lane filters, so this field-level divergence is unguarded in both directions. Consumers that read these members (`rebuttal.mjs:420 upheldCount`, `fix-brief.mjs:178`) already tolerate the shape, hence minor.

samples.summary: The ancestor write-check can refuse every `--out` run on systems with umask 002, where home directories are group-writable 0775
samples.evidence: `unsafeBaseReason(..., { leaf: false })` uses `forbidden = 0o022` and only exempts sticky directories. On Debian/Ubuntu-style user-private-group setups with umask 002, `$HOME` and project directories are commonly mode 0775 — group-writable, non-sticky — so `--out ~/review` (and any base under such a directory) fails with `refusing to use the review directory …: its ancestor /home/dev — it is writable by another user and not sticky`, which is wrong for a user-private group and gives the developer no way forward. The default (`os.tmpdir()`) path is unaffected because /tmp is sticky, so this only bites `--out` users; worth either allowing a group-writable ancestor whose gid matches the caller's own group, or naming the fix in the message.

verdict.reason: The claimed code is present exactly as described. scripts/agent/spec-to-pr.mjs:867-871 deletes every round-N directory under the base when --fresh is passed; :878 then forces `onDisk = []`, so :879 `nextRound([])` yields 1 (:185), and :886-887 `roundBoundNotice(1)` returns "" (:226) so the `if (notice && !args.force) return fail(notice)` refusal never fires. At round 1 the carry-forward is skipped entirely (:930 and dry-run :898 both gate `priorFindingsFor` on `round > 1`), and the run can end at :996 printing "no blocking findings (round 1)" on a base whose round-3 blockers were just deleted. No guard rejects or warns about --fresh past the bound: reviewArgsError (:587-597) validates only --out/--round/--rebuttals, and `args.fresh` appears nowhere else in cmdReview. The flag is reachable and advertised (:30, :1008 usage; docs/tasks/active/20260917-self-review-loop-todo.md:57,103). The code's own comment at :880-885 claims "--force is the override … and --fresh is not it — that discards the carry-forward", i.e. the implementation contradicts its stated contract. This is a reachable bypass of a newly-enforced guard plus loss of the carry-forward invariant other rounds depend on — in-lane and blocking. Only the reviewer's quote from .claude/commands/self-review.md could not be checked (that file is absent from this working tree), but it is peripheral to the defect.
